description: Kansas — "Sunflower State" — entered the Union 1861 (34th). Its capital is Topeka and its largest city is Wichita. Kansa and Osage; Bleeding Kansas. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Kansas achieved statehood 1861 (34th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Wheat and cattle; Dust Bowl. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Kansas its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Kansas went from territory to state.
definition: How Kansas went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Kansas: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Aviation (Wichita). Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Kansas's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Topeka
d: Topeka is the capital of Kansas.
definition: Topeka is the capital of Kansas.
description: Topeka has been the seat of Kansas government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Kansas's largest is Wichita — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Sunflower State
description: The nickname "Sunflower State" captures how Kansas sees itself — and how America sees it. Wichita became the Air Capital of the World. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Ad astra per aspera (To the stars through difficulties)."
